record.original_question: Let Ω be the tiling space of an aperiodic repetitive tiling of dimension d, and let p(n) count patches of radius n up to translation. If p(n)=O(n^d), must the rational Čech cohomology of Ω be finitely generated, equivalently must rk(H^*(Ω,Q)) be finite?

evidence.quote: In higher dimensions, the complexity function of a tiling counts in an analogous way the number of patches of radius n (up to translation).
Problem 2.5.1. With the same notation, is it the case that for an aperiodic, repetitive tiling of dimension d, if p(n) = O(nd), then rk(H ∗ (Ω, Q)) < ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite local complexity (only finitely many patches of any given size up to translation). Assume $\mathcal{T}$ is:
- aperiodic: no nonzero vector $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfies $\mathcal{T}+v=\mathcal{T}$; and
- repetitive: for every patch $P$ of $\mathcal{T}$, there exists $R>0$ such that every ball of radius $R$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a translated copy of $P$.

Let $\Omega$ denote the tiling space (continuous hull) of $\mathcal{T}$, namely the closure of the orbit $\{\mathcal{T}-v : v\in\mathbb{R}^d\}$ in the natural metric topology where two tilings are close if they agree on a large ball around the origin after a small translation.

Define the complexity function $p(n)$ to be the number of patches of $\mathcal{T}$ of radius $n$, counted up to translation.

Question: If $p(n)=O(n^d)$, must the rational Čech cohomology $H^*(\Omega,\mathbb{Q})$ be finitely generated, equivalently, must $\mathrm{rk}\,H^*(\Omega,\mathbb{Q})<\infty$?
artifact.category_tag: aperiodic tiling spaces and Čech cohomology
artifact.status_search_result: No source explicitly resolves this question. Related results show that for restricted classes (e.g., rational projection patterns, almost canonical tilings, certain hierarchical/substitution tilings) the Čech cohomology of the hull is finitely generated, but a general implication "polynomial complexity of order $n^d$ $\Rightarrow$ finite total Betti number" for aperiodic repetitive FLC tilings does not appear to have been established or refuted in the literature located.

status_evidence.title: Integral cohomology of rational projection method patterns
status_evidence.snippet: For rational projection patterns, the Čech cohomology is finitely generated.
status_evidence.claim: Finite generation is known in special restricted families, not in the general polynomial-complexity setting.

status_evidence.title: Cohomology of Hierarchical Tilings
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of cohomological tools for hierarchical/substitution tilings.
status_evidence.claim: Finite generation is known for substitution/hierarchical tilings, but the general polynomial-complexity question is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: Tilings, tiling spaces and topology (Sadun survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing complexity functions and Čech cohomology of tiling spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Survey-level treatment that does not provide a resolution to the polynomial complexity vs finite-rank cohomology question.
